claims.text: Oxidation resistance and material integrity in multiprincipal-element alloys are governed by preferential surface enrichment of protective elements such as Al or Cr.
Surface-enriched Al or Cr forms a continuous, slow-growing, adherent protective oxide scale.
Insufficient enrichment of protective elements permits formation of non-protective, porous, or volatile MnO- or V2O5-based scales.
Non-protective Mn- or V-containing oxide scales lead to rapid oxidation and material degradation.
Mn can become the major oxide-forming element in an equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi alloy and produce non-protective oxides and bulk Mn depletion.
The proposed baseline alloy does not inherently segregate enough protective elements to form a protective scale.
Increasing the Al or Cr concentration will increase protective-element surface segregation and promote formation of a stable protective oxide.
A controlled high-temperature pre-anneal can promote protective-element surface segregation and subsequent formation of a protective oxide.
A continuous spinel, Al2O3, or Cr2O3 scale acts as a barrier to oxygen ingress.
During high-temperature exposure, protective elements segregate to the surface and oxidize into a dense, adherent barrier.
The dense oxide barrier suppresses rapid oxygen diffusion.
The protective barrier minimizes formation of volatile or porous oxides from rapidly diffusing elements.
Without sufficient protective-element enrichment, fast-diffusing elements dominate oxidation and cause breakaway oxidation.
The modified alloy will have lower oxidation mass gain than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will form thinner, more uniform oxide scales than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will retain mechanical properties better after oxidation than the baseline alloy.
The baseline alloy will form thicker, porous, discontinuous oxide layers and undergo accelerated degradation of mechanical integrity.
The proposed governing behavior should apply in air from 600 to 900 degrees Celsius for exposures up to approximately 100 hours.
At lower temperatures or substantially longer exposures, additional oxidation mechanisms may become important.
The threshold protective-element enrichment required for a fully protective scale has not been quantitatively established.
